stem: What radiographic procedure is recommended for a child showing clinical features of rickets?
explanation: An X-ray of the left wrist is the standard view used to look for metaphyseal widening, fraying, or cupping.
rationale: One specific limb joint is the standard for checking metaphysical changes.

optionExplanations.A: While the rosary is a physical sign, the definitive radiographic changes are best seen in the growth plates of the extremities.
optionExplanations.B: An X-ray of the left wrist is the standard view used to look for metaphyseal widening, fraying, or cupping.
optionExplanations.C: While ankles can show signs, the wrist is the preferred and most standardized site for investigating rickets.
optionExplanations.D: A full skeletal survey is generally unnecessary for the initial diagnosis of rickets when localized X-rays suffice.

source.hint: One specific limb joint is the standard for checking metaphysical changes.
